intro.title: Build mock server for third party dependencies
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple mock server using Node.js to simulate third-party API dependencies, allowing you to test your applications without relying on external services. You'll learn how to create an HTTP server that responds to requests with predefined data, mimicking real API behavior. The core concepts include using Node.js's built-in 'http' module to handle requests and responses, and structuring mock endpoints. By the end, you'll have a functional mock server that returns JSON data, helping you develop and test independently.
intro.usecase: Mock servers are essential when developing applications that depend on external APIs or services that are unreliable, rate-limited, or still in development. For example, when building a payment processing dashboard that integrates with Stripe or PayPal, developers can create mock endpoints to simulate transaction responses without hitting production APIs. This allows frontend teams to build UI components like transaction tables and payment status panels while backend services are being developed. Similarly, e-commerce platforms use mock servers to simulate inventory management APIs, enabling developers to test product listing pages and shopping cart functionality independently. This pattern ensures development can continue smoothly even when third-party dependencies are unavailable or unstable.
